transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-24
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Omar Reyes (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Patel (Harbor Head of Data), Liam O'Connor (Harbor IT Security), Sofia Morales (Harbor DevOps), Ethan Brooks (Director, AI Ops)

Summary: First discovery for air-gapped / on-prem Redwood Private. Focus on regulated pharma constraints (no egress, offline updates), hardware sizing, SSO/KMS/ audit logging, and pilot scope. Customer leaning to fully air-gapped private deploy but evaluating tradeoffs vs Dedicated.

Topics: on-prem air-gapped requirements, offline update procedures, hardware constraints (GPU types, NVMe), latency/cost tradeoffs, security controls (SOC2/ISO, KMS/HSM, SSO), deployment automation, rollback and fallback strategies.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, AE on the account, with Omar from our SE team. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Dr. Priya Patel: Good thanks. We wanted to use this time to talk about how Redwood would run inside our network — specifically air-gapped environment.
[00:15] Omar Reyes: Great. I have a checklist we'll walk through. Quick high-level questions first: are you looking for fully offline with zero internet egress, or is limited outbound to a known update host acceptable?
[00:28] Liam O'Connor: Full air-gap is the aim. We have regulatory audits — no outbound except via our controlled jumpbox process. Updates must be via signed artefacts transferred on removable media or a controlled update server.
[00:38] Sofia Morales: Yep, and we want to avoid any callouts to public cloud endpoints. Even telemetry needs to be optional and retained on-prem.
[00:44] Omar Reyes: Understood. Redwood Private supports an air-gapped deployment mode. Practically that looks like: control plane in your VPC or offline control plane, local inference nodes behind your firewall, and a signed bundle for model and runtime updates. We also provide scripts to orchestrate transfers via jumpbox.
[01:02] Ethan Brooks: How do you handle model updates? Say a model patch or a quantized checkpoint — how do we verify integrity?
[01:09] Omar Reyes: We produce signed bundles with SHA256 checksums. The bundle includes a provenance manifest and optional signature via a customer HSM. There's a verification step in the offline installer. We can also support dedupe+delta patches to keep transfer sizes down.
[01:23] Dr. Priya Patel: Good. Bandwidth is limited — our facility links are a bit old. We'll need to plan for multi-GB model transfers over a secured USB or internal file share.
[01:33] Maya Chen: We typically recommend quantized model variants for air-gapped installs to reduce transfer size. Also, we can precompute a delta patch from your current version to the next, often cutting the transfer by 70-90% depending on change set.
[01:48] [00:60] Liam O'Connor: What's the runtime footprint? We're trying to figure out how many GPUs and what flavor. We have some NVIDIA A10s and a couple of A100s, and one older T4 cluster.
[01:58] Omar Reyes: For throughput targets, can you share a target qps and average prompt lengths? That drives batch sizing and GPU needs.
[02:05] Sofia Morales: We're targeting 50 qps for internal tooling in phase 1, with average request ~2k tokens, peak bursts to 120 qps. Latency SLO is 500ms 95th for simple completions, some longer for long-form generation.
[02:18] Omar Reyes: 2k token average is heavy. For that, A100s or H100s are recommended. A10s will work for smaller models or heavy quantization but you'll trade latency. For 50 qps at 2k tokens, expect to need a cluster of several A100s — we'll share a sizing spreadsheet. The T4s are unlikely to meet your latency SLO for that token size unless you accept higher latency.
[02:38] Dr. Priya Patel: Is that because of memory/KV cache limits?
[02:42] Omar Reyes: Exactly. Longer contexts keep larger KV caches and more memory bandwidth. Also kernel selection for attention matters. Our runtime will pick fused kernels where available but hardware makes a big difference.
[02:52] [03:00] Ethan Brooks: Regarding security — do you support customer KMS integration? We use HashiCorp Vault and an HSM for key wrapping.
[03:08] Omar Reyes: Yes. We integrate with KMIP/HSM and can plug in Vault for envelope encryption. Keys can be provisioned and stored on your HSM; Redwood won't hold unwrapped keys for air-gapped installs.
[03:19] Liam O'Connor: Audit logs — retention and where they live? We need immutable logging for forensics and compliance for seven years.
[03:26] Maya Chen: Audit logs are local, with option to ship to your SIEM. For air-gapped, logs remain in your environment. We support append-only write patterns and signed log rotation. We'll include a log schema and retention configuration.
[03:39] [03:45] Dr. Priya Patel: What about SSO and RBAC? We'll need SCIM provisioning and SAML 2.0.
[03:49] Omar Reyes: SAML 2.0 and SCIM supported in Private. For fully air-gapped, SCIM can be proxied via your identity bridge or we can provide a manual provisioning API. RBAC maps to roles you configure; we can add fine-grained permissions for model access, deploy rights, and audit review.
[04:05] Sofia Morales: Can we automate deploys? We have an internal pipeline that handles config-as-code — we'd like Terraform or Ansible steps.
[04:12] Omar Reyes: We provide Terraform modules and Ansible playbooks for the Private deploy. For air-gapped installs, the playbooks include steps to load signed bundles from local storage and verify signatures.
[04:21] [04:30] Ethan Brooks: Is there a fallback option in case a local node dies? We don't want a single point of failure.
[04:34] Omar Reyes: Typically you deploy across multiple racks or AZ-equivalents, with an HA proxy and multiple replica inference workers. For air-gapped, failover is local; we can support async replication of KV caches to speed cold-starts, but that involves internal network traffic only.
[04:48] Maya Chen: Quick question on telemetry — for debugging, sometimes we need metrics. In air-gapped mode is limited telemetry allowed?
[04:55] Liam O'Connor: We only allow metrics that are aggregated and don't include customer PII or prompt data. Exported to our internal Prometheus endpoint.
[05:03] Omar Reyes: We can run a prometheus exporter and agree on metrics whitelist. All logs with prompt content can be disabled by default.
[05:11] [05:20] Dr. Priya Patel: Cost wise, what's the delta between Dedicated reserved capacity and Private air-gapped? We need ballpark to go to finance.
[05:25] Maya Chen: Ballpark — hosted is lowest operational lift but higher per-token costs; Dedicated reserved capacity gives predictable throughput and lower per-token cost with isolation; Private air-gapped has higher one-time deployment and support costs (on-prem licensing, installation, on-call) plus hardware CAPEX. We'll send a comparison sheet with estimated TCO over 3 years.
[05:45] Sofia Morales: Are there managed options where Redwood helps with on-prem updates but we keep the cluster isolated?
[05:50] Maya Chen: Yes — we call that 'air-gapped managed' where you control the network but we provide signed bundles and remote support via a jumpbox process or scheduled physical transfer. For the most regulated setups you choose the manual update path.
[06:03] [06:10] Ethan Brooks: I'm worried about model provenance — we need to ensure the model hasn't been tampered with and is the exact open model we expect. Also we may want a completely vetted model snapshot.
[06:20] Omar Reyes: We ship model manifests with source references, checksums, and optionally a notarized provenance token. For enterprise customers we can provide an audit trail of the model build, quantization steps, and the exact runtime version used.
[06:35] Dr. Priya Patel: Great. On governance — if we detect model quality regressions during the pilot, can we pin older versions and roll back quickly?
[06:42] Omar Reyes: Yes; rollbacks are supported. Our deploy system keeps previous artifacts and can perform in-place rollbacks. For air-gapped installs it's a local action and uses the same signed bundles.
[06:50] [07:00] Liam O'Connor: A couple of compliance specifics: do you support data residency tagging and guaranteed prompt retention deletion on request?
[07:07] Maya Chen: For Private installs, data never leaves your environment unless you opt-in; retention policies are configurable and we have APIs to delete stored artifacts. We'll provide the retention/deletion API docs.
[07:19] Sofia Morales: Operational question — how long to stand up the environment from our side? We have windows for maintenance.
[07:25] Omar Reyes: Typical on-prem air-gapped install with full validation and security reviews takes 4–8 weeks depending on scheduling and access to hardware; smaller pilot nodes can be done in 2–3 weeks. We'll put a timeline in the POC proposal.
[07:39] [07:45] Dr. Priya Patel: For the pilot, what would you propose as success criteria?
[07:49] Maya Chen: Suggested POC: 6 weeks; scope: deploy Private instance in your lab, run a simulated workload (~50 qps, 2k tokens average), validate latency SLOs, security checklist (no egress, KMS integration, audit logging), and run a small eval set for quality/regression. Success = 95th pctl latency < 600ms for defined calls and security checklist completed.
[08:09] Ethan Brooks: Sounds reasonable. Will we need Redwood on site for installation?
[08:13] Omar Reyes: Not usually — most installs are remote with your DevOps doing the install. For the first install we offer optional on-site assistance for an extra fee.
[08:20] [08:30] Dr. Priya Patel: Any gotchas with older GPU drivers or CUDA versions? Our cluster uses mixed driver versions.
[08:35] Omar Reyes: We recommend consolidated driver stacks; mixed drivers can complicate scheduling and runtime optimizations. We provide a compatibility matrix. For mixed environments we can containerize inference nodes but performance tuning may be needed.
[08:48] Maya Chen: Going to recap next steps — we'll send the security pack, a hardware sizing spreadsheet, and a pricing TCO comparison. Omar will prepare the SE deep-dive and sizing for next week.
[08:59] [09:00] Dr. Priya Patel: Great. Also we'll send over our internal list of compliance questions and a network diagram for the facility.
[09:07] Sofia Morales: I'll add the allowed jumpbox IPs and our maintenance window to the diagram.
[09:12] Maya Chen: Perfect. Any other questions?
[09:15] Liam O'Connor: One last quick question — any recommended quantization strategy to balance perf and accuracy?
[09:20] Omar Reyes: We usually recommend per-tensor 4-bit quant for LLMs where you need throughput but preserve key layers in higher precision — mixed quantization. We'll run a small eval on your prompts during the POC to pick the sweet spot.
[09:33] [09:40] Dr. Priya Patel: That covers it. Thanks everyone.
[09:42] Maya Chen: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the docs and schedule the deep-dive for 2026-03-31.
